html:
SMTO-WEB-0010 — SMTO's web reader can't read this kind of file

GUID: 3511c334-ac0e-41ea-9674-745a98425068
Slug: web-unsupported-content-type
Domain: WEB · Subsystem: web

What happened

  • The address returned something other than a web page, plain text or PDF, such as an image, video or download file, or an error in a form SMTO can't read. SMTO didn't use it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the address in your own browser to see what it shows. If it's an error or missing page, give SMTO the correct address. Sites often send their error pages in forms the web reader doesn't accept.
  2. If the address is a file such as an image, spreadsheet or archive, ask SMTO to download it and open it with the matching tool instead of reading it as a web page. The web reader only handles web pages, plain text, simple data files and PDF files.
  3. If you need the information rather than that exact file, ask SMTO to find a web page or PDF that contains it. A readable page lets SMTO quote the content reliably.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reads the new page, or the matching tool opens the file and shows its contents.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the address, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't treat this address as a source for the answer until something has actually read it.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Web reader rejected the response because its Content-Type is not HTML, XHTML, plain text, JSON or PDF.

What this means

  • The response Content-Type is outside the Web reader's supported text and document representations. The diagnostic adds no retrieval. Read outcomes and retained receipts determine what evidence is available; an error does not establish the content of an unread source.

Why this can happen

  • The response Content-Type is outside the Web reader's supported text and document representations.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the recorded media type and choose a capability that supports that representation.

How to fix it

  • read_page in src/agent_runtime/skills/web/reader.py accepts text/html, application/xhtml+xml, text/plain and application/json (plus application/pdf or octet-stream on 2xx for document acquisition); check the recorded content_type and status_code. Use the HTTP download or file tools for other representations; an unsupported body on a 4xx/5xx is a completed observation, not page evidence.
  • Use an appropriate native HTTP or file capability for the representation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The selected capability produces readable evidence for the actual content type.

What not to do

  • Do not treat an unsupported response body as readable evidence.

Technical notes

  • The diagnostic adds no retrieval. Read outcomes and retained receipts determine what evidence is available; an error does not establish the content of an unread source.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
